title: Add release-please workflow and config
description: Add .github/workflows/release-please.yml using googleapis/release-please-action, plus release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json, configured for this Python package (release-type: python, tracking pyproject.toml's version). unhoard already uses conventional commits (enforced by the /commit skill), so release-please can derive version bumps and changelog entries from commit history with no behavior change to the commit workflow itself.

title: Add CI workflow: mypy + pytest on push/PR
description: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml that installs dependencies, runs mypy, and runs the pytest suite on push and pull_request. Depends on the mypy config existing (unhoard-7p6.1) and the pytest scaffolding existing (unhoard-d70.1) so there's something real for the workflow to run.

title: CLI/integration tests for unhoard commands
description: Exercise unhoard's CLI entry points end-to-end (init, sync, digest, mark, apply, stats, synthesize) against fixtures/mocked sources, asserting on exit codes and output. Cover the interactive-picker vs. non-tty fallback behavior in mark/apply when a key fragment matches multiple items.

title: Unit tests for summarize.py and digest.py
description: Cover the Anthropic summarization call (mocked, no real API calls), the content-hash cache-invalidation logic (including invalidation when 'context' changes), and digest.py's bucketing/rendering (new/aging/stale caps, tag+collection suggestion formatting, digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md + latest.md output).

title: Unit tests for config.py, state.py, schema.py
description: Cover config loading/merging (file + UNHOARD_* env vars), state persistence (marking done/unhoarded/snoozed, sync reconciliation when an item disappears from its source), and schema validation/bucketing logic (new/aging/stale by day thresholds).

title: Unit tests for source adapters (Raindrop, Chrome, Safari, JSON)
description: Cover unhoard/sources.py: Raindrop API pagination/auth with mocked HTTP, Chrome bookmarks+reading-list JSON parsing, Safari Bookmarks.plist parsing, and the generic JSON source's field-guessing/field_map override behavior. Mock the filesystem and network -- no real API calls or real browser profile reads in tests.

title: Set up pytest scaffolding and dev dependencies
description: Add pytest (plus pytest-mock and an HTTP-mocking library like responses, since sources.py hits Raindrop's API) as dev dependencies. Establish tests/ layout, conftest.py with shared fixtures (tmp config dir, isolated state DB/file, fake Raindrop responses), and a documented way to run the suite locally. This unblocks all the module-specific test tasks below.

title: Add type hints to sources.py, summarize.py, digest.py
description: Add full type annotations to unhoard/sources.py (the Raindrop/Chrome/Safari/JSON source adapters), unhoard/summarize.py (Anthropic summarization calls and caching), and unhoard/digest.py (bucketing/rendering logic).

title: Add type hints to cli.py and ui.py
description: Add full type annotations to unhoard/cli.py (argparse/command wiring) and unhoard/ui.py (rich/questionary output helpers), completing coverage across the whole package.

title: Add type hints to config.py, state.py, schema.py
description: Add full type annotations (function signatures, dataclass/attrs fields, return types) to unhoard/config.py, unhoard/state.py, and unhoard/schema.py using the typing module. These are the foundational data-layer modules other modules depend on, so typing them first gives the most leverage for catching downstream errors.

title: Add mypy dev dependency and config
description: Add mypy as a dev dependency and a [tool.mypy] section in pyproject.toml (start permissive -- e.g. ignore_missing_imports for questionary/trafilatura/rich -- so it doesn't immediately fail on untyped third-party deps). Add a way to run it locally (e.g. documented command or script entry). This is the foundation the per-module typing tasks and the CI type-check job build on.

title: Add GitHub Actions: CI + release-please automation
description: unhoard has no .github/workflows at all -- no CI and no release automation. Add a CI workflow that runs type checking and tests on push/PR, and a release-please workflow to automate versioning, changelog generation, and GitHub releases from the project's conventional commits.

title: Add static typing to unhoard with the typing module
description: unhoard currently has zero type hints across its modules (config.py, digest.py, ui.py, summarize.py, sources.py, cli.py, state.py, schema.py) and no static type checker. Add type hints using Python's typing module throughout, plus mypy wired in so regressions get caught automatically (and later in CI).

title: Add automated test suite (pytest)
description: unhoard has no automated tests at all. Add a pytest-based test suite covering config/state/schema, the source adapters (Raindrop/Chrome/Safari/JSON), summarize/digest (including the content-hash caching logic), and the CLI commands, so regressions are caught before they ship.

title: Add 'unhoard synthesize' to pull full article content into a standalone note
description:
New command: 'unhoard synthesize <key>'. Pulls the full article text (reusing summarize.py's fetch_article_text(), already used for AI summaries -- same trafilatura extraction, no new fetch logic needed) and writes it as a standalone markdown note, giving the user real material to work with when actually doing the synthesis for an old-web-style project (or any PKM use), rather than just a link.

Design:
- Output path: <output_dir>/synthesized/<slug>.md (subfolder next to the digest files, not mixed in with digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md/latest.md). Slug derived from the item title (lowercased, non-alphanumeric collapsed to hyphens, reasonable length cap).
- Note content: YAML frontmatter (title, url, source, key, tags, synthesized_at date) then, if a cached AI summary exists for the item, a short 'Summary' section, then a 'Full Text' section with the fetched article content.
- Safety: check whether the target file already exists on disk before writing -- if so, skip and warn rather than overwriting, since the user may have already started expanding/editing that note by hand. Add a --force flag to explicitly overwrite when that's actually wanted.
- Distinct from 'mark --unhoarded': synthesize just pulls raw material in for the user to work with; --unhoarded is the separate, later step of recording that the material was actually used somewhere with proper attribution (--note). Don't auto-mark unhoarded here.
- Track synthesized_at locally (new state.py column, parallel to tags_applied_at/collection_applied_at/summary_applied_at) so stats/future digest logic can know an item already has a synthesis note -- the overwrite-safety check itself should still be a real file-existence check on disk, not just this DB flag, so it stays correct even if the DB and filesystem ever drift.
- If fetch_article_text() comes back empty (no trafilatura, fetch failure, or no URL), warn and don't write an empty note.

Follows the CLI conventions established in unhoard-e5b: rich-styled success/warning output, escaped dynamic content (titles/paths can contain brackets).
close_reason: Added 'unhoard synthesize <key> [--force]'. Fetches full article text via summarize.py's existing fetch_article_text() (same trafilatura path already used for AI summaries) and writes a standalone note to <output_dir>/synthesized/<slug>.md with YAML frontmatter (title/url/source/key/tags/synthesized_at) plus a Summary section (if a cached AI summary exists) and the full text. Frontmatter strings/arrays are built with json.dumps(), which produces valid YAML flow scalars/sequences -- verified round-tripping a title with brackets, colons, and quotes through a real YAML parser. Won't overwrite an existing note unless --force is passed (real file-existence check, not just the new synthesized_at DB column, which is informational only). Empty/unfetchable article text fails cleanly with exit 1 instead of writing a useless note. Distinct from mark --unhoarded, which stays a separate, later step.

title: Show friendly help instead of an argparse error when 'unhoard' is run with no command
description:
'uv run unhoard' with no subcommand currently produces:

  usage: unhoard [-h] {init,sync,digest,mark,apply,stats} ...
  unhoard: error: the following arguments are required: command

That's argparse's default behavior for a required subparser with nothing given -- a bare usage line plus a scary 'error:' message, no indication of what unhoard actually does or which command to run first. Every subcommand already has a decent --help string; the fix is just to surface the full help output (which lists them all with descriptions) instead of the terse error.

Fix: stop marking the subparsers 'required' in build_parser(), and in main(), when args.command is None, print the full parser help and return a non-zero exit code (nothing was done, matches the spirit of the old behavior) instead of falling through to a crash or silently doing nothing.
notes: Correction before this shipped: the first implementation routed format_help() through rich.markup.escape() + console.print(), which double-processed Python 3.14's argparse's own ANSI color codes (argparse gained built-in color=True help formatting, gated on _colorize.can_colorize()'s tty detection) into visible garbage escape sequences in a real terminal -- confirmed by forcing can_colorize() to return True and comparing outputs. Fixed to call parser.print_help() directly, bypassing rich's markup pipeline entirely so argparse's own color handling (or lack thereof) passes through untouched.
close_reason: Dropped required=True from the subparsers and added an explicit args.command is None check in main() that prints the full parser help (via format_help(), escaped and routed through the shared rich Console for consistency) and returns 1, instead of argparse's bare 'error: the following arguments are required' message. --help and actual invalid-command errors are unaffected.

title: Interactive picker for ambiguous 'mark'/'apply' key matches
description:
Today, _find_single_item() (cli.py) prints a list of matches and returns None (exit 1) when a key fragment matches more than one item -- the user has to re-run the command with a longer fragment. Use questionary.select() to let them pick interactively instead, when running in a real terminal.

Guard on sys.stdin.isatty() (and probably sys.stdout.isatty()) -- cron jobs and scripts piping output must keep today's exact behavior (print the list, exit 1) since there's no one there to answer a prompt. Only offer the interactive picker when both are ttys.

This only touches _find_single_item()'s ambiguous-match branch -- the no-match branch (nothing found at all) has nothing to pick from and stays as todays's error message regardless of TTY.

Depends on unhoard-e5b.1 for the questionary dependency being in place.
close_reason: Added _is_interactive() (sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()) gate in _find_single_item(). When both are true and there's an ambiguous match, uses questionary.select() to let the user pick interactively; a cancelled picker (Ctrl-C/Esc, .ask() returns None) is treated the same as no match. Non-interactive contexts (cron, scripts, piped, and this sandboxed environment itself) keep the exact old behavior: print the list, return None, exit 1 -- verified against a real subprocess with no attached tty, plus mocked-isatty tests for the select/cancel/unambiguous-skips-picker paths. Full command regression unaffected.

title: Render digest --print as Markdown + progress bar for stale-item summarization
description:
Two digest.py-focused improvements:

1. 'unhoard digest --print' currently dumps the raw markdown source to the terminal. Render it through rich.markdown.Markdown instead so headers/links/emphasis actually display formatted in the terminal. The saved digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md/latest.md files are unaffected -- they stay plain markdown text for cron/scripts/Claude Code to read; only the interactive --print preview changes.

2. Add a rich.progress bar/spinner around the stale-item loop in build_digest (digest.py) when cfg.anthropic_enabled and there's actual summarization work to do (reuse the existing _needs_fresh_summary check from unhoard-7mt.2 -- don't show a progress bar if everything's already cached, matching the existing zero-network-call-when-cached behavior). Each stale item that needs summarizing involves a real network fetch + an Anthropic API call, so a silent multi-second pause for a handful of items is exactly the kind of thing a progress indicator is for.

Depends on unhoard-e5b.1 for the shared Console.
close_reason:
digest --print now renders through rich.markdown.Markdown instead of dumping raw source; saved digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md/latest.md files are unaffected (same build_digest() output, just rendered differently at print time). Added a rich.progress bar around the stale-item loop, gated by the same needs_fresh check that already controls collection-name fetching -- no bar shown on a fully-cached digest.

Along the way, fixed a real markdown-structure bug this surfaced: <sub> tags and lazy blockquote continuation (no '>' prefix on the Action line) were causing Summary/Action/suggestion/key to merge into one garbled paragraph under any real CommonMark renderer -- previously invisible because --print just dumped raw markdown source. Restructured each stale/aging/new item into properly blank-line-separated blocks (bullet header, blockquote, suggestion line, key line, each as *emphasis* instead of raw <sub> HTML) and collapsed Summary+Action onto one line to avoid blockquote soft-break ambiguity. This fixes both the new --print rendering and the previously-broken structure of the saved .md files themselves. Verified: rendered output structure, raw saved file structure, piped/non-TTY --print (clean degradation, single-line progress bar summary, no ANSI codes), and full command regression.

title: Rich-format output for sync, mark, apply, stats, and init
description:
Migrate the simpler commands to the new ui.py helpers (unhoard-e5b.1):

- sync: colored per-source lines (green check on success, red on failure), styled summary line.
- mark / apply: green success messages, yellow warnings (no write-back support, missing suggestions, etc.), red errors -- same information as today, just visually distinguishable at a glance instead of everything being the same plain text.
- stats: render as a rich.table.Table (status counts, active-by-source counts) instead of manually formatted print lines.
- init: styled panel or colored sections for the 'Next steps' output instead of a single plain print block.

No behavior changes -- same information, same exit codes, just legible. Verify piped/non-TTY output (e.g. 'unhoard stats | cat') still degrades to plain readable text rather than raw ANSI codes or a broken table -- rich handles this automatically via Console but worth confirming.
close_reason: Migrated init/sync/mark/apply/stats to ui.py's Console/print_success/print_warning/print_error. init's next-steps now render in a rich Panel; stats renders as two rich Tables (by status, active-by-source) instead of manual print lines. Escaped all dynamic content (item titles, error messages, source names, collection titles, tags, config paths) via rich.markup.escape() since titles/collections come from arbitrary web content and Raindrop collections that can contain literal brackets -- verified this explicitly with a bracket/angle-bracket-laden title through mark and apply, nothing broke. digest.py/cmd_digest untouched (that's e5b.3). Verified piped/non-TTY output (stats | cat) degrades to plain box-drawing text with no raw ANSI codes, same exit codes and information as before throughout.

title: Add rich + questionary dependencies and a shared UI helper module
description:
Foundational for the rest of this epic:

- 'uv add rich questionary' -- adds both to pyproject.toml/uv.lock.
- New unhoard/ui.py module exporting a single shared rich.console.Console instance and small helpers for consistent styling across commands, e.g. print_success(msg), print_warning(msg), print_error(msg) (green/yellow/red, all going through the shared Console so color detection/no-color-when-piped works consistently everywhere rather than each command deciding independently).
- Every command currently mixes stdout print() for normal output and stderr print(..., file=sys.stderr) for errors/warnings -- keep that stdout/stderr split (important for scripting/cron), just route both through the new Console (Console(stderr=True) for the error one) instead of bare print().

Nothing user-visible changes yet in this issue beyond having the plumbing in place -- actual command output gets migrated to use it in the next issue.
close_reason: Added rich and questionary as dependencies (uv add rich questionary -- resolved cleanly, questionary had no prompt_toolkit conflicts unlike PyInquirer would have). New unhoard/ui.py with a shared Console (stdout) + err_console (stderr) and print_success/print_warning/print_error helpers. No command output migrated yet -- that's e5b.2. Verified rich correctly auto-detects non-TTY output and strips ANSI codes when piped, and that questionary imports cleanly. Existing CLI behavior unaffected.

title: Make the CLI more user-friendly with rich + questionary
description:
unhoard's CLI is currently plain print()/stderr text throughout -- no color, no formatting, digest --print dumps raw markdown source instead of rendering it, ambiguous 'mark <key>' matches just print a list and fail rather than letting you pick, and there's no progress indicator during digest's AI summarization loop even though it makes real per-item network calls.

Libraries (confirmed with user): rich for styled output/tables/progress bars/markdown rendering, questionary for interactive prompts (chosen over PyInquirer, which is unmaintained since ~2019 and has a prompt_toolkit pin that conflicts with modern Python). Not using alive-progress -- rich's built-in progress bars cover that need without a second dependency doing the same job.

Scope is CLI presentation only -- no behavior changes to sync/digest/mark/apply logic, just how their output looks and how ambiguous input is handled. The saved digest-YYYY-MM-DD.md/latest.md files stay plain markdown; only the --print terminal preview gets richer rendering.

Child issues, in dependency order: add the two dependencies + a shared console/UI helper module, rich-format the simpler commands (sync/mark/apply/stats/init), render digest --print as Markdown + add a progress bar for the summarization loop, add interactive picking for ambiguous key matches, and docs.
close_reason: All five child issues complete: rich + questionary dependencies with a shared ui.py module, rich-formatted sync/mark/apply/stats/init output, digest --print rendered as Markdown with a progress bar (plus a real markdown-structure bug fix this surfaced), a TTY-gated interactive picker for ambiguous key matches via questionary, and docs.

title: New 'unhoard apply' command to push suggestions/summary to Raindrop on demand
description:
New CLI surface, separate from 'mark': 'unhoard apply <key> [--tags] [--collection] [--summary] [--all]'.

Behavior:
- Reads the item's stored suggested_tags / suggested_collection / summary from local state (unhoard-7mt.2).
- For --collection, resolve the suggested collection NAME to an id via the adapter's list_collections() (unhoard-7mt.1) -- if it doesn't match any real collection (or is 'none'), skip with a message rather than erroring.
- Calls the adapter's apply_updates() (unhoard-7mt.1) with whichever subset of {tags, collection_id, note=summary} was requested via flags.
- Best-effort, same philosophy as mark --unhoarded: if the source has no write-back support or the call fails, print a warning and exit 0 rather than hard-failing -- there's no local state to fall back to here (this command IS the write-back), so a failure here is just a failure, but it shouldn't look like a crash.
- Open question to resolve during implementation: should applying something be recorded locally (e.g. tags_applied_at / collection_applied_at / summary_applied_at) so re-running digest / stats can show what's already been pushed, and so it's visible that an item's suggestions were acted on? Lean toward yes -- otherwise there's no record that --apply ever ran on an item, which matters once digest is re-summarizing (unhoard-77w's context-change cache-busting) and might regenerate different suggestions later.

Depends on both adapter capabilities (unhoard-7mt.1) and the suggestion fields existing to read from (unhoard-7mt.2).
close_reason: Added 'unhoard apply <key> [--tags] [--collection] [--summary] [--all]'. Resolves suggested tags/collection from local state, matches collection name to id via list_collections() (case-insensitive, skips gracefully if the collection no longer exists), writes the AI summary as a note. Best-effort like mark --unhoarded: no write-back support or a failed API call both exit cleanly with a message. Added mark_applied() tracking (tags_applied_at/collection_applied_at/summary_applied_at) so the digest stops suggesting things already pushed -- resolves the open design question in favor of tracking. Factored the repeated 'find item by key' logic out of cmd_mark into _find_single_item(), reused by cmd_apply. Verified: happy path, no-suggestions warning, stale/deleted collection name, no-write-back source, unknown key, and the digest suppression of already-applied suggestions -- all via mocked adapters, no live API calls.

title: Extend AI prompt + parsing to suggest tags and a grounded target collection
description:
Today the whole AI response (Summary + Action lines) is stored and rendered as one opaque text blob -- summarize.py returns raw text, digest.py just displays it verbatim. Extending this to also suggest tags and a collection requires actually parsing the response into fields for the first time.

Scope:
- Extend PROMPT_TEMPLATE (summarize.py) to also ask for 'Tags: <comma-separated>' and 'Collection: <one of the existing collection names below, or none>' lines, alongside the current Summary/Action.
- Pass the real list of the user's Raindrop collections (from unhoard-7mt.1's list_collections()) into the prompt so the model picks from actual collections instead of inventing plausible-sounding ones that don't exist. This is Raindrop-specific -- sources without collections (chrome/safari/json) just don't get a collection suggestion; leave that line out of the prompt for those, or always pass an empty list and let 'none' be the only option.
- Add a small parser (e.g. parse_summary_response(text) -> dict with summary/action/tags/collection keys) rather than continuing to treat the response as an undifferentiated blob.
- New state.py columns: suggested_tags (TEXT, comma-separated or JSON), suggested_collection (TEXT, a name not an id -- resolution to id happens at apply time in unhoard-7mt.3).
- digest.py's stale-item rendering shows the suggestions alongside Summary/Action so the user can see them before deciding whether to apply anything.

Depends on unhoard-7mt.1 for the collection list this needs to ground suggestions in reality.
close_reason: Extended PROMPT_TEMPLATE to ask for Tags/Collection lines grounded in the real Raindrop collection list (fetched once per digest run, only when at least one stale item actually needs fresh summarization). Added parse_summary_response() to structure the AI reply instead of treating it as an opaque blob. New suggested_tags/suggested_collection columns in state.py. digest.py stores a clean Summary+Action body (no duplication) plus a separate suggestion line pointing at the future 'unhoard apply' command. Verified: parser edge cases, full digest flow with mocked Anthropic+Raindrop calls, zero-network-call re-run on fully cached items, and the no-Raindrop-adapter fallback (chrome items still get Summary/Action, no collection grounding).

title: RaindropAdapter: list_collections() + generalized apply-updates write-back
description:
Two capabilities the rest of this epic depends on:

1. list_collections() -> list[{'id': int, 'title': str}] via Raindrop's GET /rest/v1/collections (and /rest/v1/collections/childrens if nested collections should be included -- decide during implementation whether to flatten or just cover top-level). Used by: the AI prompt extension (to ground collection suggestions in real names) and the apply command (to resolve a suggested collection NAME back to the ID Raindrop's write API actually needs).

2. Generalize the tag/collection/note write logic currently embedded in mark_unhoarded() into a reusable method, e.g. apply_updates(source_id, tags=None, collection_id=None, note=None) -> None, that merges tags (not replace, same as today), optionally moves collection, optionally sets note. mark_unhoarded() should become a thin wrapper that calls apply_updates() with self.unhoarded_tag added to tags and self.unhoarded_collection_id as collection_id -- so applying suggested tags/collection/summary via the new 'apply' command doesn't require going through the unhoarded status at all.

Note the shared 'note' field nuance: apply_updates(note=...) will overwrite whatever note is currently on the Raindrop item (Raindrop only has one note field). Both mark --unhoarded --note and the future apply --summary write through this same path -- last write wins. No special handling needed here, just don't lose sight of it in method naming/docs.
close_reason: Added RaindropAdapter.apply_updates() (generalized partial update: tags merge, collection move, note set -- any subset) and list_collections() (flattens top-level + nested via /collections and /collections/childrens). mark_unhoarded() is now a thin wrapper over apply_updates(). Extended WritebackAdapter protocol in base.py to match. Verified with mocked HTTP sessions: regression on mark_unhoarded, tags-only/note-only/no-op apply_updates paths, and collection listing -- no live API calls.

title: Suggest tags + destination collection, apply AI output to Raindrop on demand
description:
Building on the unhoarded write-back plumbing (unhoard-s4k): extend the stale-item AI summarization call to also suggest tags and a destination collection for each item, shown in the digest alongside the existing Summary/Action. Then add a new 'unhoard apply <key>' command that pushes any combination of {suggested tags, suggested collection, the AI summary text} back to Raindrop on demand -- nothing here writes anything automatically, same opt-in philosophy as --unhoarded.

Design decisions locked in with the user:
- Suggestions are generated automatically during the normal 'digest' run (extending the existing per-stale-item AI call), not a separate on-demand generation step.
- Applying suggestions is a NEW command, 'unhoard apply', not folded into 'unhoard mark'. Keeps 'mark' about local state transitions (done/unhoarded/snooze) and 'apply' about pushing AI output to the source.

Open nuance to carry into implementation: 'mark --unhoarded --note' and 'apply --summary' both ultimately write to Raindrop's single per-item 'note' field, from two different local columns (user citation vs AI summary text). Last write wins -- document this clearly rather than silently surprising the user.

Child issues, in dependency order: Raindrop adapter capabilities (list_collections + generalized write-back), AI prompt/parsing extension (needs the collection list to ground suggestions), the apply CLI command, and docs.
close_reason: All four child issues complete: Raindrop adapter capabilities (list_collections + generalized apply_updates), AI prompt/parsing extension for grounded tag/collection suggestions, the 'unhoard apply' command with applied-state tracking, and docs.

title: Wire 'unhoard mark --unhoarded' to trigger source write-back
description:
Glue work: cmd_mark in cli.py currently only touches local state (StateStore). Once --unhoarded exists locally and adapters can optionally write back, cmd_mark needs to:
1. Look up which source the matched item belongs to (row['source']).
2. Build (or reuse) the right adapter instance for that source -- note sources.build_adapters() currently builds *all* configured adapters from config.toml, there's no existing helper to get 'just the raindrop one for this item'. May need a small addition there.
3. If that adapter supports mark_unhoarded (hasattr check), call it with the item's source_id and note. If it fails (network, auth, etc.) or the adapter doesn't support write-back, the local state change should still succeed -- print a warning, don't hard-fail. Local state is the source of truth for unhoard itself; source write-back is best-effort enrichment.

Depends on both the local-state and adapter/Raindrop issues.
close_reason: Added find_adapter_for_source() in sources.py and wired it into cmd_mark's --unhoarded path in cli.py. Write-back is best-effort: no adapter match or an exception both degrade to a stderr warning while the local state change (source of truth) still succeeds. Verified all three paths (write-back success, no-support source, write-back failure) with mocked/patched adapters -- no live Raindrop API calls made.

title: Adapter write-back protocol + Raindrop tag/collection implementation
description:
Adapters are currently fetch-only (adapters/base.py Protocol only defines fetch()). To reflect 'unhoarded' back in Raindrop we need an optional write path.

Scope:
- Extend the Adapter protocol with an optional write-back method, e.g. mark_unhoarded(source_id: str, note: str | None) -> None. Adapters that can't support it (chrome, safari, generic_json -- all local read-only exports/files) simply don't implement it; callers must check via hasattr/getattr rather than assuming every adapter supports it.
- Implement it on RaindropAdapter using Raindrop's PUT /rest/v1/raindrop/{id} endpoint: add a configurable tag (default 'unhoarded', via new config field e.g. unhoarded_tag) to the item's existing tags, and if an unhoarded_collection_id is configured, also move the raindrop to that collection.
- Stretch: if a note is provided, consider writing it into Raindrop's own per-raindrop 'note' field too, so the citation is visible in Raindrop itself and not just local sqlite.
- New config fields: unhoarded_tag (default 'unhoarded'), unhoarded_collection_id (optional, default unset = tag-only behavior).

Depends on the local state issue for the 'note' concept it needs to pass through, but the Raindrop API call itself can be built and tested independently (RaindropAdapter already holds an authenticated session).
close_reason: Added WritebackAdapter protocol (base.py), RaindropAdapter.mark_unhoarded() that merges the configurable tag into existing tags and optionally moves to a collection, plus config fields (unhoarded_tag, unhoarded_collection_id) wired through sources.py. Verified with a mocked HTTP session -- no live API calls made.

title: Define 'unhoarded' as local state distinct from 'done'
description:
Right now 'unhoard mark <key> --done' means 'stop showing me this' whether that's because you ignored it or because you actually did something with it. We need to distinguish 'unhoarded' (synthesized + stored + properly sourced elsewhere) from plain 'done' (just closing it out).

Proposed shape:
- Add an 'unhoarded_at' timestamp column (or a distinct status_reason value) to the items table in state.py, separate from the existing done/snoozed/active status enum -- decide during implementation which fits the schema better.
- Add a 'note' column to capture provenance/citation: where/how the item was used (e.g. 'folded into the CSS-tricks retrospective page, linked back to original'). This is the 'properly sourced' half of the definition -- an unhoarded item without a note is only half-unhoarded.
- Extend 'unhoard mark <key>' with a new '--unhoarded' flag (alongside existing --done/--snooze), requiring or strongly encouraging a '--note "..."' alongside it.
- 'stats' command should probably break out unhoarded counts separately from generic done counts.

This is the local-state half of the feature; source write-back is a separate dependent issue.

title: Write back an 'unhoarded' marker to source apps
description:
unhoard is currently read-only against every source (README: 'Nothing is ever deleted by this tool. It only reads.'). The local 'done' status conflates two very different outcomes: 'I decided I don't care' and 'I actually synthesized/stored/cited this material somewhere.' We want the second case -- call it 'unhoarded' -- to be a distinct, source-visible signal, not just a row in local sqlite.

Definition of 'unhoarded' (the working definition of what this tool means by archive): some action was taken to synthesize and store the information from this item, AND it was properly sourced/cited, elsewhere (e.g. folded into an old-web-style project with attribution back to the original).

For Raindrop specifically, represent this via a tag (e.g. 'unhoarded') and/or moving the raindrop to a dedicated collection -- make it configurable rather than picking one mechanism, since either is a reasonable way to see it reflected in the Raindrop UI.

This changes unhoard's read-only design tenet. The README needs updating to something like: 'never deletes anything, but can optionally write a small marker back to the source when you explicitly say an item has been unhoarded.'

Child issues break this into: local state model, adapter write-back capability + Raindrop implementation, CLI wiring, and docs.
close_reason: All four child issues complete: local unhoarded state + note field, WritebackAdapter protocol + Raindrop tag/collection implementation, CLI wiring with best-effort write-back, and README docs.

title: Add user context to stale-item summarization prompt
description: The digest's AI summarizer recommends Delete/Archive purely from article content, with no awareness of the user's own projects/interests. This misfires on things like archived old-web tutorials the user is deliberately collecting as reference material for old-web-style site work -- they read as 'outdated' but are wanted. Add a free-text 'context' config setting that gets included in the summarization prompt, and bust the cached-summary check when the context changes so already-summarized stale items get re-evaluated under the new rule.
close_reason: Added context config field, threaded through prompt + cache-busting

Separate repo, lower priority, and possibly a manual step is fine for now -- exploratory.

title: unhoard init output doesn't mention context or unhoarded config
description:
cmd_init's printed 'Next steps' (cli.py) only covers RAINDROP_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, [[sources]], sync, and digest. It says nothing about the 'context' setting (added for stale-item summarization, see unhoard-77w) or unhoarded_tag/unhoarded_collection_id (added for the write-back feature, unhoard-s4k and children) -- even though write_default_config already writes commented-out examples for both into config.toml. A first-time user running 'unhoard init' has no way to discover these from the CLI output alone; they'd have to go read the generated config.toml comments or the README.

Fix: extend the printed next-steps in cmd_init to mention that config.toml has commented examples for context (contextualizes AI summary recommendations against the user's own projects) and unhoarded_tag/unhoarded_collection_id (controls how mark --unhoarded writes back to Raindrop), pointing at the relevant config.toml section rather than repeating the full docs inline.
close_reason: Extended cmd_init's next-steps to point at config.toml's commented-out context and unhoarded_tag/unhoarded_collection_id examples instead of staying silent about them.

title: README: revise read-only claim now that unhoarded write-back exists
description:
README currently says 'Nothing is ever deleted by this tool. It only reads.' Once mark --unhoarded can write a tag/collection change back to Raindrop, that claim is no longer accurate. Update it to something like: unhoard never deletes anything on its own, but marking an item --unhoarded can optionally write a small marker (tag and/or collection move) back to a source that supports it, and only when you explicitly ask for it via CLI. Also document the new config fields (unhoarded_tag, unhoarded_collection_id) and the --unhoarded/--note mark flags in the Config Reference and Daily Use sections.

Depends on the CLI wiring issue being done so the docs describe real behavior.
close_reason: Revised the read-only claim, added a 'What Unhoarded Means' section explaining the done vs. unhoarded distinction and write-back behavior, added --unhoarded example to Daily Use, and documented unhoarded_tag/unhoarded_collection_id in Config Reference.
